name: St Basil the Great
title: Archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia
summary: A brilliant student who became a bishop, fed the hungry, built a city of mercy for the sick, and bravely defended the faith before the emperor's men.
sourceNote: The text for older readers follows the Life of St Basil in St Dimitri of Rostov's Lives of the Saints (January 1), retold in our own English words. The story of the Vasilopita is a later, beloved tradition and is marked as such. Draft — awaiting review.

athens.caption: In Athens, Basil and his best friend Gregory study together: they know only two roads — to church and to school.
athens.alt: The city of Athens with marble temples on a hill, olive trees and cypresses. Young Basil and Gregory, carrying scrolls and books, walk side by side up a stone road toward a church, while students debate under a portico and goats graze nearby.

famine.caption: During a terrible famine, Basil cooks for the hungry and serves them with his own hands.
famine.alt: A courtyard in Caesarea with great steaming cooking pots over fires. Basil in his priestly robes ladles soup into the bowls of a long line of poor people, children and old men, while helpers carry baskets of bread and a new hospital with many windows stands in the background.

modestus.caption: Basil is not afraid of the prefect Modestus: "Perhaps you have never met a bishop before!"
modestus.alt: Inside a stone hall in Caesarea, the angry prefect Modestus in a rich purple cloak points and shouts, surrounded by soldiers. Bishop Basil, thin and calm, with a dark beard and a white omophorion with crosses, stands peacefully holding the Gospel.
